target: def Target (𝓑 : S₀) (K : Fm → Fm) : Prop := ∀ φ, 𝓑 ⊢ K φ 🡒 K (K φ)
a_raw: {"translation":"For any sentence type Fm with the given connectives and constants, any system type S₀ with a provability relation on Fm, any system 𝓑 of type S₀, and any function K from Fm to Fm, Target(𝓑, K) is defined to mean that for every sentence φ, 𝓑 proves the object-language implication (K φ) 🡒 K(K φ). It is the implication itself that must be provable for each φ; there is no premise that 𝓑 proves φ or K φ, and neither the antecedent nor the consequent is required to be separately provable. No classicality or consistency assumption on 𝓑 is made."}
translation: For any sentence type Fm with the given connectives and constants, any system type S₀ with a provability relation on Fm, any system 𝓑 of type S₀, and any function K from Fm to Fm, Target(𝓑, K) is defined to mean that for every sentence φ, 𝓑 proves the object-language implication (K φ) 🡒 K(K φ). It is the implication itself that must be provable for each φ; there is no premise that 𝓑 proves φ or K φ, and neither the antecedent nor the consequent is required to be separately provable. No classicality or consistency assumption on 𝓑 is made.

divergences.description: The target uses an abstract sentence type and operator rather than Reinhardt’s arithmetic formulas with the constructor B. It therefore does not represent the universal closures of instances in which p has free variables.
The target requires each instance to be provable in 𝓑, without distinguishing an adopted axiom, as in the passage, from a derived theorem.

judgement.summary: For closed sentences, the target faithfully captures the unprefixed schema Bp → BBp: it is the implication itself that 𝓑 must prove. It does not require the optional B prefix.
